summary: Proves a positive, well-defined primary mixed-multiplicity kernel at arbitrary characteristic and residue field. This is an algebraic result, without geometric intersection or locality conclusions.
detailedSummary: Establishes symmetry, product/power linearity, single-slot monotonicity by simultaneous superficial choices, integral-closure invariance by a finite graded algebra argument, and all-support valuative well-definedness. Finite residue-field transfer is algebraic only. Unit slots have zero moments and lower-dimensional components contribute zero under the declared degree-n convention.
text:
Use n1. Write e_R(I_1,...,I_n) for the coefficient with one entry of each primary ideal in the degree-n part of the multigraded length polynomial.

The exact current July 2024 Swanson–Huneke author source is retained locally. Complete Theorem 17.4.2 and Definition 17.4.3 give the polynomial for finite modules over arbitrary Noetherian local rings, with degree equal to the module dimension and degree-dim R mixed coefficients zero for smaller-dimensional modules. Complete 17.2.2 gives superficial choices in nonempty Zariski opens, with prescribed finite prime avoidance. Complete 17.2.4 and 17.4.6 give reduction of a mixed coefficient by a superficial element avoiding minimal primes, without Cohen–Macaulay or reduced quotient assumptions. Complete 8.4.2 permits the algebraic extension R(Z)=R[Z] localized at mR[Z]: dimension, primary ideals and finite lengths are preserved. A finite-length composition series tensors to one whose factors are kappa(m)(Z), proving length preservation directly. This extension is used only for algebraic proofs; no boundary identification across it is assumed.

Symmetry follows by relabelling polynomial variables. Substituting equal variables for I and J represents (IJ)^t. The coefficient with exponent one in this shared variable receives exactly the terms having exponent one in I or in J. Consequently e(IJ,I_2,...,I_n)=e(I,I_2,...,I_n)+e(J,I_2,...,I_n), and substitution t↦rt gives e(I^r,I_2,...,I_n)=r e(I,I_2,...,I_n). A unit slot contributes zero because the length polynomial is independent of its variable.

Here is single-slot monotonicity without a false coefficientwise inference from polynomial inequalities. Suppose J⊂K and fix the other n−1 ideals. Over an infinite residue field choose an element in I_2 superficial for BOTH tuples (I_2,I_3,...,I_n,J) and (I_2,I_3,...,I_n,K), avoiding all minimal primes. The complete 17.2.2 proof makes the allowed choices complements of finitely many proper vector subspaces of I_2/mI_2. Their intersection has a point over an infinite field. Quotient dimension drops by one: avoiding minimal primes gives the upper bound; lifting a parameter system from the quotient and applying the height theorem gives the lower bound. Both included ideals remain primary in the quotient. Apply 17.4.6 to both tuples and repeat in the remaining fixed slots. At dimension one, J^N⊂K^N gives length(R/J^N)≥length(R/K^N); dividing by N gives e(J)≥e(K). Hence e(J,I_2,...,I_n)≥e(K,I_2,...,I_n) in every dimension. Reducing a tuple of primary slots to a one-dimensional primary multiplicity also proves positivity. The complete one-variable Hilbert–Samuel statement/proof and positive leading coefficient, 11.1.3–5, were read. The nonreduced intermediate quotients are allowed by these sources.

Integral-closure invariance is separate. If K⊂overline(J), let L=J+K. Homogeneous ideal-integrality equations make R[Lt] finite graded over R[Jt]. Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most h. Their degree t+h coefficients give L^(t+h)⊂J^t for all t≥1. Also J^t⊂L^t. Multiplying by A=I_2^(t_2)...I_s^(t_s) gives
length(R/L^t A)≤length(R/J^t A)≤length(R/L^(t+h) A).
Along any ray of positive integral exponents, divide by the common parameter to power n. The fixed shift h does not change the top homogeneous part, so the top parts for J and L agree on every positive rational ray and hence as polynomials. Thus all relevant mixed coefficients agree. If J and K have equal integral closure, apply this argument to J+K from both sides. This requires neither normalized Rees-algebra finiteness nor coefficientwise monotonicity of arbitrary polynomial differences.

For primary-or-unit ideals, the exact all-support criterion is
v(K)≥v(J) on X_a iff K⊂overline(J).
For proper primary J, apply complete Swanson–Huneke 6.8.4 to each local domain R/P, P minimal. Each has positive dimension, and the image of a is nonzero primary. Normalizing its centred rank-one DVRs by a makes them actual boundary points. Complete 6.8.3 or 1.1.5 assembles componentwise integral dependence. Conversely, a monic ideal-integrality equation and the unique-smallest-term argument prove the value inequality after quotienting by ANY semivaluation support. Primary values are finite. Unit cases are immediate or impossible as appropriate. Using minimal-support DVRs to prove the criterion does not remove other supports from the domain.

For rational inputs u_i=−v(I_i)/k_i define
B_u(v(J))=e_R(I_1,...,I_p,J)/(k_1...k_p).
For p=0 this is e_R(J); a zero input represented by the unit gives zero for p≥1. Equal profiles, after integer powers, give equal ideal values, hence equal integral closures. Invariance and power linearity prove presentation independence. Every rational relation among ideal tests becomes v(A)=v(B) after synchronizing denominators and multiplying ideals, so the test functional is well-defined. If v(A)−v(B)≥0, then A⊂overline(B), A+B has the same integral closure as B, and inclusion monotonicity gives e(I_1,...,I_p,A)≥e(I_1,...,I_p,B). Therefore the functional is positive on the entire rational test lattice.

Input order follows as well: u≤w makes ideal-gauge moments for u at least those for w. For u=−v(I)/k and w=−v(J)/l, use I^l⊂overline(J^k) and divide the resulting inequality by kl. Addition of negative rational profiles corresponds to product ideals and is additive in each slot.

These arguments discharge the algebraic kernel independently of ROOT338. They do not prove independent Cartier intersection comparison or locality. Exact bodies, hashes, URLs and complete immediate application units are in inputs/primary and source-application-ledger.md. Rerun: python audit_inputs.py; python build_delivery.py. Execution is not mathematical verification.
